STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a flat white plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall or bowl shadow. It is a flat plate, roughly square with rounded corners.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: the plate looks like a square-ish dinner plate, typically 20-30 cm. The plate is fairly large relative to the food, so I'd place it medium-large, around 26 cm.
b) Reference cue: the pizza slice is about 11-12 cm along its crust edge, and the plate spans roughly two to two-and-a-half slice lengths across its width. That gives about 24-27 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm (square plate, side length 25 cm).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Pizza: one slice visible (about 1/6 to 1/8 of a 30 cm pizza, roughly 1/6 of a whole pie). Estimated slice mass about 100 g. Visible toppings: mushrooms, red onion, olives, tomato sauce, cheese. Count the slice as one piece, approx 100 g.
- Chicken and vegetables (stir-fry style): footprint covers roughly 35% of the plate. Plate area = 25 x 25 = 625 cm²; food footprint ≈ 0.35 x 625 ≈ 220 cm². Thickness: chicken pieces are about 2 cm, stacked about 2 deep at the thickest point, mound averages about half the peak, so average thickness ≈ 1.5-2 cm. Volume ≈ 220 x 1.75 ≈ 385 ml. Density about 1.0 g/ml, giving ≈ 300-350 g of chicken and vegetables with sauce. Split: chicken about 230 g, Brussels sprouts, zucchini and yellow squash about 100 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the pizza sits on the plate with no base layer. Under the stir-fry there is a thin sauce film, already included. No additional hidden layer is needed.

STEP 5 - Energy values (as served):
- Pizza with cheese, tomato and vegetable toppings: about 260 kcal per 100 g.
- Chicken stir-fry meat (fried/glazed chicken pieces with sauce): about 190 kcal per 100 g.
- Mixed vegetables (Brussels sprouts, zucchini, squash, peppers) cooked in oil: about 70 kcal per 100 g.

Totals: pizza about 100 g x 2.6 = 260 kcal; chicken 230 g x 1.9 ≈ 437 kcal; vegetables 100 g x 0.7 = 70 kcal. Total about 770 kcal from roughly 430 g of food.
